kai: quick loop — ran a narrowband slice (short multi-turn customer-help queries) for nova-lite-8b (int4) vs our baseline opt7b-int8. putting the headline numbers here, want routing + GTN handoff guidance.

lena: drop the headline deltas pls.

kai: TL;DR:
- latency (p95, cold): nova-lite-8b-int4 = 85ms, opt7b-int8 = 120ms (≈29% faster)
- throughput (tokens/s per GPU): nova-lite = 4200, opt7b = 3000
- cost per 1k tokens (in our infra estimate): nova-lite ≈ $0.0058, opt7b ≈ $0.0086 (≈32% lower)
- quality (slice-specific): exact-match on QA-style short prompts: opt7b = 82.4%, nova-lite = 79.1% (Δ = -3.3pp)
- hallucination rate (auto-check semantics): opt7b = 4.1%, nova-lite = 5.3% (Δ = +1.2pp)
- notable regression buckets: numeric-prefilled answers and multi-step clarification prompts (examples below)

zoe: ok that quality drop is non-trivial for support flows. what’s the slice size / eval set?

kai: 1,200 samples drawn from production narrowband traffic (turns <= 3, avg tokens/request ≈ 38). we stratified by intent: 60% faq, 25% account ops, 15% escalation.

ajay: any latency-tail issues? p99?

kai: p99 nova-lite = 210ms, opt7b = 310ms. tail follows same ratio. KV-cache hit tests (local prefix cache) improve p95 to ~60ms for nova-lite when hit.

lena: can you paste a tiny example of a failure? short please.

kai: example (aggregated):
- prompt: "Why did my charge duplicate on 3/9? I already disputed once."
- opt7b: correctly cites last 4 digits + escalation step, asks clarifying Q (good)
- nova-lite: returns plausible but incorrect charge date and omits escalation guidance (hallucination)

ajay: routing thought: this seems like a good candidate for hybrid routing where nova-lite serves low-risk FAQ/short reads and opt7b covers account ops + escalations. fallback to opt7b on low-confidence / hallucination signals.

zoe: agreed. do we have an automated confidence/hallucination signal to act on?

kai: we have two lightweight signals we tested: perplexity delta vs prompt baseline (threshold) and a fast answer-checker (surface match to knowledge base). combining them gives ≈78% precision for catching these failures.

ajay: propose config sketch for routing (ops-friendly):
```
route {
  match: request.slice == "narrowband_short" && request.turns <= 3
  primary: "nova-lite-8b-int4"
  fallback_on: ["low_confidence", "kb_mismatch"]
  fallback_to: "opt7b-int8"
  traffic_split: { default: 0.9 primary, 0.1 canary }
}
```

lena: for GTN/product talking points: we can position as "fast-lite" with clear caveats — <30% cost saving and ~30% latency improvement on narrow short-turn queries, but measurable small regressions on multi-step/account ops. recommend A/B with explicit rollback criteria.

ops-bot: deploy-bot: canary rollout started for nova-lite-8b-int4 in eng-sandbox (id: canary-6187654321) :rocket:

kai: recommended handoff checklist to product/GTN + oncall:
- Start canary at 10% narrowband_short traffic for 14 days.
- Monitor: slice EM, hallucination signal, p95 latency, and rate of fallback triggers.
- Auto-fallback policy: if hallucination signal > 1.5pp over baseline OR fallback triggers > 5% of requests for 24h -> rollback to opt7b.
- Data capture: log prompts flagged by confidence checker + final outputs for human review.
- Eval cadence: run daily 200-sample QA check on flagged prompts, weekly 1k sample full slice audit.

zoe: GTN note: for marketing, push cost/latency story but require "guardrails" language in playbook. recommend we prepare a short FAQ (2 bullets) on where nova-lite should NOT be used (billing/account auth/escalations).

ajay: operational config snippet for automated fallback (pseudo):
```
if (confidence < 0.36 || kb_match == false) {
  route.to(opt7b)
  emit("replay_for_audit")
}
```

kai: next steps: implement routing rule + enable replay logging. I'll push a short dashboard (latency + fallback rate + quality delta) and tag you all. can we get GTN to approve messaging by EOD Wed?

lena: yes, I’ll draft GTN copy and send to @zoe + @ajay for signoff. :thumbsup:

zoe: sounds good. one more ask — can we run a small 5k user parallel A/B to validate cost saving estimate in prod telemetry before wide rollout?

kai: yep I’ll schedule that for next sprint and attach experiment id to canary logs.

ops-bot: note: incident-runbook updated with fallback thresholds (link: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/quant-routing)

ajay: thanks — this feels actionable.

lena: thanks everyone, will sync on GTN copy tomorrow. :white_check_mark:
